decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display is a low-cost catalog variant close to the core offer, and keeping it listed preserves a flexible option while demand after the pandemic years is still unclear.
The pegboard-back display uses existing cardboard capabilities and costs little to hold, so there is no conclusive evidence yet that justifies giving up the option.
The standard quarter-pallet display is a core format with steady demand and negligible holding cost, so it stays on the market.
The wooden pallet costs more to sustain and lies outside the paper core, but it remains a diversification option with uncertain value, especially as interest in sustainable materials grows.
The media display serves a shrinking niche, but it costs little to keep listed and can be repurposed, so the option stays open for now while we watch closely for abandonment.
